caption: A steel bolt is tossed toward a strong magnet fixed to a workbench, and the bolt swerves and clacks onto the magnet.

sa.check: A magnet fixed to a workbench.
A steel bolt is tossed toward the magnet.
The bolt's flight swerves toward the magnet.
The bolt lands on the magnet and stays there.
The bolt travels through the air: it is thrown, not placed by hand.
The toss comes first, the swerve follows, then the landing.

pc.expect: The bolt flies from the toss along a downward-sagging arc; as it nears the magnet its path bends toward the magnet and ends on its surface.
pc.fail: The bolt bends away from the magnet; or flies past it and then turns back; or curves toward a place on the bench other than the magnet and stops there.

pc.expect: On contact the bolt stops on the magnet and stays there; the magnet stays fixed to the bench and the bolt does not move again.
pc.fail: The bolt bounces off the magnet and lands away from it; or keeps sliding across the magnet after landing; or drops off the magnet while nothing touches it; or the magnet shifts on the bench when the bolt hits.

pc.expect: The flight sags downward; a bolt that misses falls to the bench or floor; a bolt on the magnet stays held even on the magnet's side.
pc.fail: The bolt climbs steadily through its flight with no downward arc; or hangs in the air; or a missed bolt floats instead of falling.

pc.expect: The bolt stays a rigid piece of steel and does not bend or squash on hitting the magnet; the magnet and bench keep their shape.
pc.fail: The bolt bends or crumples on impact; or the magnet's face dents where the bolt hits; or the bench surface ripples.

pc.expect: One bolt and one magnet fixed to the bench; the bolt does not pass into the magnet or the bench, does not split and does not vanish.
pc.fail: The bolt vanishes in flight; or two bolts appear; or the bolt sinks into the magnet or through the bench; or the magnet leaves the bench and follows the bolt.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The magnet's colour, the bench top and the tools on it stay the same; the bolt keeps its size.
pc.fail: The magnet changes colour or shape; or tools on the bench move or vanish; or the bolt changes size between toss and landing.
